thesis: Audit four types of professional time before redesigning a workday.
summary: Bloom distinguishes management, creation, consumption and ideation. Batch necessary coordination into discrete windows; protect creation when energy is high; deliberately consume varied inputs; and leave stimulus-free space to connect ideas. His exercise is a week of calendar color-coding followed by rebuilding one more balanced day. He acknowledges less calendar control early in a career.

insights.title: Distinguish coordination from creation and inputs
insights.explanation: The model names four uses of professional attention rather than treating all busyness as equivalent.

insights.explanation: Management is acknowledged as real work; batching is intended to keep it from consuming every available block.

review_status: Codex editorial draft; complete local transcript read; claims not independently verified
synthesis_method: Direct Codex extraction from complete local transcript; exact quotations verified locally
context_and_limits: Personal scheduling model, not an experimentally validated universal productivity intervention. Management is necessary and may require multiple windows. His hours and equipment are examples; consumption and ideation do not require a sauna, and consuming more is not itself creating.
review_changes: Adds the actual diagnostic exercise, necessary management work, varied consumption and deliberate absence of input for ideation.
